### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive issue title

### Description
<!-- A description of the bug or feature -->
There're a direct memory leaks in AcquireMagickMemory of MagickCore/memory.c:478:10 and 
many indirect memory leaks.

### Steps to Reproduce
<!-- List of steps, sample code, failing test or link to a project that reproduces the behavior.

`magick -seed 0 "(" magick:netscape +repage ")" "(" magick:granite +repage ")" -append -fft -compare   tmp`

cmd:

# Run build preparation scripts if they exist

  if [ -x "$prep_script" ]; then
    echo "Running $prep_script..."
    ./$prep_script
    break
  elif [ -f "$prep_script" ]; then
    echo "Found $prep_script but it's not executable, setting permissions..."
    chmod +x $prep_script
    ./$prep_script
    break
  fi
done

# Handle different build systems
if [ -f "configure" ]; then
  echo "Found configure script, running with options: $CONFIG_OPTS"
  ./configure $CONFIG_OPTS

  echo "Building with make $MAKE_OPTS"
  make $MAKE_OPTS

  echo "Found CMakeLists.txt, using CMake build system"
  mkdir -p $BUILD_DIR
  cd $BUILD_DIR
  cmake $CMAKE_OPTS ..
  make $MAKE_OPTS

  echo "Found Makefile, building with make $MAKE_OPTS"
  make $MAKE_OPTS
elif [ -f "meson.build" ]; then
  echo "Found meson.build, using Meson build system"

  cd $BUILD_DIR

  echo "Found GNUmakefile, building with make $MAKE_OPTS"
  make $MAKE_OPTS

  make $MAKE_OPTS

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR yara.cve-2017-5924..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /src/yara/yara /testcase/yara_uaf_yr_compiler_destroy.yar strings
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/yara
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    
    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi
    
    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi
    
    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \n         1>/dev/null \n         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR gpac.cve-2023-0841..."
    # Run the MP4Box command with the PoC file
    /src/gpac/bin/gcc/MP4Box -info /testcase/mp3_dmx_process_poc2

    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/gpac
    
    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with patch."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi
    
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"

payload.build_sh:
#!/bin/bash

# Check if bootstrap.sh exists and is executable
if [ -f ./bootstrap.sh ]; then
    chmod +x ./bootstrap.sh
    ./bootstrap.sh
fi

# Set compiler flags
export CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -fsanitize=address"
export CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -fsanitize=address"

# Run configure script
if [ -f ./configure ]; then
    ./configure --enable-macho --enable-debug --enable-dex --enable-dotnet --without-crypto
fi

# Clean and build the project
make clean -j$(nproc)
make -j$(nproc)
payload.secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR yara.cve-2016-10211..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /src/yara/yara /testcase/yara_uaf.yar strings
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/yara
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
# Minimized build script with only core build commands
set -e

# Navigate to the mruby source directory
cd /src/mruby

# Set the linker to clang
export LD=clang

# Set linker flags
export LDFLAGS="-w -Wno-yacc -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types -fsanitize=address -fsanitize-address-use-after-scope"

# Build the project using rake with multiple processors
rake -m -j$(nproc)
payload.secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /src/mruby/build/host/bin/mruby /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/mruby

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
# Default build script template for C/C++ projects
set -eu

# Define configuration options
CONFIG_OPTS="--disable-shared"
CMAKE_OPTS="-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug"
MAKE_OPTS="-j$(nproc)"
BUILD_DIR="build"

# 1. Run build preparation scripts if they exist
for prep_script in buildconf autogen.sh bootstrap; do
  if [ -x "$prep_script" ]; then
    echo "Running $prep_script..."
    ./$prep_script
    break
  elif [ -f "$prep_script" ]; then
    echo "Found $prep_script but it's not executable, setting permissions..."
    chmod +x $prep_script
    ./$prep_script
    break
  fi
done

# Clean the project before building
if [ -f "Makefile" ] || [ -f "makefile" ]; then
  echo "Cleaning project with make clean"
  make clean || true
fi

# 2. Handle different build systems
if [ -f "configure" ]; then
  echo "Found configure script, running with options: $CONFIG_OPTS"
  ./configure $CONFIG_OPTS

  echo "Building with make $MAKE_OPTS"
  make $MAKE_OPTS
elif [ -f "CMakeLists.txt" ]; then
  echo "Found CMakeLists.txt, using CMake build system"
  mkdir -p $BUILD_DIR
  cd $BUILD_DIR
  cmake $CMAKE_OPTS ..
  make $MAKE_OPTS
elif [ -f "Makefile" ] || [ -f "makefile" ]; then
  echo "Found Makefile, building with make $MAKE_OPTS"
  make $MAKE_OPTS
elif [ -f "meson.build" ]; then
  echo "Found meson.build, using Meson build system"
  mkdir -p $BUILD_DIR
  meson setup $BUILD_DIR .
  cd $BUILD_DIR

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

    USE_ZEND_ALLOC=0 /src/php-src/sapi/cli/php /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/php-src

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

payload.bug_description: mrb_ary_shift_m in src/array.c fails to validate negative shift counts. A negative shift value can be used when constructing/indexing the array storage, leading to an out-of-bounds/invalid memory read (segmentation fault). This can be triggered via array shift operations with negative arguments, causing crashes and other memory-safety issues (denial-of-service).

    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive

        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"

    unlimited length. This meant that when pdf_map_one_to_many() from commit
    6b0a8273f2eb15fd5924501b6ad03e30f2c8d0a started to handle surrogate pairs
    of more than two characters it might advance past the end of the string
    causing the reported issue.

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /work/bin/exrcheck -c -s /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/openexr

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

            patch "$@"

else

fi

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /out/mupdf/mutool draw -o /tmp/out.png /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."

else

fi

payload.patch:
commit 74e920a40e0aea93f7cefca6e6bbff249d637b18
Author: Sebastian Rasmussen <sebras@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 13 07:11:01 2023 +0100

    Use the correct buffer size when parsing cmap.
    
    pdf_parse_bf_range_array() lexes a hex string, converts it
    into binary and passes it to pdf_map_one_to_many().
    
    To handle fuzzed files commit a6b0a8273f2eb15fd5924501b6ad03e30f2c8d0a
    introduced a limit of the binary to 256 bytes. But instead of passing the
    (possibly limited) string length to pdf_map_one_to_many() it passed the
    unlimited length. This meant that when pdf_map_one_to_many() from commit
    6b0a8273f2eb15fd5924501b6ad03e30f2c8d0a started to handle surrogate pairs
    of more than two characters it might advance past the end of the string
    causing the reported issue.
    
    Fixes oss-fuzz issue 55051.

diff --git a/source/pdf/pdf-cmap-parse.c b/source/pdf/pdf-cmap-parse.c
index 07881da5a..d2cba367e 100644
--- a/source/pdf/pdf-cmap-parse.c
+++ b/source/pdf/pdf-cmap-parse.c
@@ -243,7 +243,7 @@ pdf_parse_bf_range_array(fz_context *ctx, pdf_cmap *cmap, fz_stream *file, pdf_l
 			for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
 				dst[i] = pdf_code_from_string(&buf->scratch[i * 2], 2);
 
-			pdf_map_one_to_many(ctx, cmap, lo, dst, buf->len / 2);
+			pdf_map_one_to_many(ctx, cmap, lo, dst, i);
 		}
 
 		lo ++;

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then

payload.secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR md4c.cve-2018-11545..."
    # Run the md2html binary with the crash_md_merge_lines test case
    /src/md4c/build/md2html/md2html /testcase/crash_md_merge_lines
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/md4c
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

commit f06afc434aec631f18f8da8ffca9a6f0559e1acf
Author: Nikita Popov <nikita.ppv@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Dec 1 11:49:27 2020 +0100

    Don't use scope when validating Attribute
    
    This is not safe to do at this point. Even if we made it safe,
    we'd see inconsistencies due to a partially compiled class.
    
    Fixes oss-fuzz #28129.

diff --git a/Zend/zend_attributes.c b/Zend/zend_attributes.c
index 29a2f4a7325..ae07802b5bc 100644
--- a/Zend/zend_attributes.c
+++ b/Zend/zend_attributes.c
@@ -33,7 +33,10 @@ void validate_attribute(zend_attribute *attr, uint32_t target, zend_class_entry
 	if (attr->argc > 0) {
 		zval flags;
 
-		if (FAILURE == zend_get_attribute_value(&flags, attr, 0, scope)) {
+		/* As this is run in the middle of compilation, fetch the attribute value without
+		 * specifying a scope. The class is not fully linked yet, and we may seen an
+		 * inconsistent state. */
+		if (FAILURE == zend_get_attribute_value(&flags, attr, 0, NULL)) {
 			return;
 		}

================= Bug Report (1/1) ==================
## Source: GitHub Issue
## URL: https://github.com/mruby/mruby/issues/4062
## Description:
Issue: mruby/mruby#4062
Title: Signed integer overflow in mrb_str_format
State: closed
Created by: clayton-shopify
Created at: 2018-06-25 15:27:56+00:00

Issue Body:
The check macro (in `/mrbgems/mruby-sprintf/src/sprintf.c`) contains an signed integer overflow in `bsize`:

```c
#define CHECK(l) do {\
/*  int cr = ENC_CODERANGE(result);*/\
  while ((l) >= bsiz - blen) {\
    bsiz*=2;\
    if (bsiz < 0) mrb_raise(mrb, E_ARGUMENT_ERROR, "too big specifier"); \
  }\
  mrb_str_resize(mrb, result, bsiz);\
/*  ENC_CODERANGE_SET(result, cr);*/\
  buf = RSTRING_PTR(result);\
} while (0)
```

`bsiz*=2` can become negative. However with `-O2` the `mrb_raise` is never triggered, since `bsiz` is a signed integer. Signed integer overflows are undefined behaviour and thus `gcc` removes the check.

This results in negative integers being passed to `mrb_str_resize`, which will set the string length without further checks. This can potentially result in a oversized string that allows to access arbitrary memory.

In our experiments building with `gcc` in version `5.4.0 20160609 (Ubuntu 5.4.0-6ubuntu1~16.04.9)` produces the vulnerable binary while `clang` generated a safe executable.

================= Bug Report (1/1) ==================
## Source: GitHub Issue
## URL: https://github.com/mruby/mruby/issues/4001
## Description:
Issue: mruby/mruby#4001
Title: Use after free in File#initilialize_copy
State: closed
Created by: clayton-shopify
Created at: 2018-04-16 15:50:03+00:00

Issue Body:
The following was reported by https://hackerone.com/pnoltof:

-----

Root Cause:
==========

calling `File#initilialize_copy` with an invalid argument, causes the function to terminate early, leaving a dangling pointer in the recievers `DATA_PTR`. 

```
mrb_io_initialize_copy(mrb_state *mrb, mrb_value copy)
{
  mrb_value orig;
  mrb_value buf;
  struct mrb_io *fptr_copy;
  struct mrb_io *fptr_orig;
  mrb_bool failed = TRUE;

  mrb_get_args(mrb, "o", &orig);
  fptr_copy = (struct mrb_io *)DATA_PTR(copy);
  if (fptr_copy != NULL) {
    fptr_finalize(mrb, fptr_copy, FALSE);
    mrb_free(mrb, fptr_copy);
  }
  fptr_copy = (struct mrb_io *)mrb_io_alloc(mrb);
  fptr_orig = io_get_open_fptr(mrb, orig); #can raise exception

  DATA_TYPE(copy) = &mrb_io_type;
  DATA_PTR(copy) = fptr_copy;
	[....]
}
```

Details & Impact
=======

initialize_copy first frees the `DATA_PTR(self)`, then it gets the data pointer for the first argument. This operation can raise an exception, in which case `DATA_PTR(self)` remains dangeling. By proper heap feng shui, one can allocate another value (such as string) in the same spot. Calling `a.close()` will set `DATA_PTR(a)->fd = -1`, effectively setting some memory to `0xffffffff`. This can be used to change the size of a string object. The corrupted string can then be used to read/write memory. This can be used to obtain arbitrary code execution.

```ruby
a = File.new(0)
#needs proper heap massaging for reallocation
a.initialize_copy(0) # DATA_PTR(a) is now pointing to free'd memory
#allocate string at old position
str = "foo".gsub("o","asdfasdf")
a.close() #overwrites offset 0 on DATA_PTR(a) with ffffffff
#str length is now 0xfffffffff, we can read/write arbitrary memory
```

Bugfix
======
Move `fptr_orig = io_get_open_fptr(mrb, orig);` to the top of the function (next to `mrb_get_args(mrb, "o", &orig);`).

Steps to Reproduce
==================

obtain current mruby version
```
git clone https://github.com/mruby/mruby.git
git checkout fabc460880fbabd18369a
CC=clang CFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -fsanitize-recover=address -ggdb -O0" LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address" LD=clang make
```

payload.bug_description: A bad-cast/UBSan error in parser.c's xmlParseElement causes a null pointer dereference (read from a near-zero address) when handling certain inputs. The invalid cast to an xmlStartTag-like structure leads to a segmentation fault and undefined behavior during parsing, which can be triggered by crafted XML and results in a denial-of-service crash.

    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then

    # stdout: /dev/null

    if /usr/local/bin/compile \

        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else

        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {

        exit 1

}

            patch "$@"
            ;;

else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"

fi

payload.bug_description: Heap-use-after-free in the mruby VM (mrb_vm_exec in src/vm.c). During certain VM execution paths (involving cipush/mrb_ary_splat and nested mrb_vm_exec calls) an object is reallocated/freed (mrb_realloc/mrb_realloc_simple) while still referenced by the VM, and the VM later reads from that freed heap memory. This can cause crashes and undefined behavior, and may enable memory corruption or further exploitation with crafted inputs.

payload.bug_description: A bounds-checking error in PackUnix::find_overlay_offset (src/p_unix.cpp) allows a 4-byte read past the end of the input buffer via the little-endian 32-bit reader (get_le32 / N_BELE_RTP::LEPolicy::get32). Malformed input can trigger a heap-buffer-overflow read during unpack detection (PackUnix::canUnpack), leading to crashes (DoS) and potential information disclosure.

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {

}

    exit 1
fi

payload.bug_description: Heap-use-after-free in the Zend VM: ZEND_FE_FETCH_RW_SPEC_VAR_HANDLER (Zend/zend_vm_execute.h) performs a read from heap memory that has already been freed. The freed region is released via zend_array_destroy (zend_hash.c) during ArrayIterator setup (ext/spl/spl_array.c, zim_ArrayIterator___construct / spl_array_set_array), but later VM bytecode handlers still access the deallocated memory. This use-after-free can cause crashes, memory corruption and may lead to further exploitation such as arbitrary code execution.

payload.bug_description: A heap-buffer-overflow in MatIO: Mat_VarPrint (src/matio/src/mat.c) calls printf/vprintf on a variable name buffer that is not guaranteed to be NUL-terminated (the buffer allocated in Mat_VarReadNextInfo4 in src/matio/src/mat4.c is 32 bytes). printf reads past the end of the allocated buffer (one byte over), causing a heap out-of-bounds read that can crash the program or lead to memory corruption and possible information disclosure or other exploitation.

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /src/libxml2/xmllint /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/libxml2

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

There is a NULL Pointer Dereference in mrb_vm_exec (vm.c:1929). This bug has been found on mruby lastest commit (hash c2f7ed514dfa0fcae2e7e72d51f25be3d3d6d72c) on Ubuntu 20.04 for x86_64/amd64.
Proof of Concept
1- Clone repo and build with ASAN using MRUBY_CONFIG=build_config/clang-asan.rb rake.
2- Use mruby to execute the poc (it is base64-encoded since it contains unprintable characters):
$ echo -ne 'Yj0iMCIKezA9Pm5pbH0KW11hbmQKYi5jb2RlcG9pbnRze2luc3RhbmNlX2V2YWx7bG9vcC5uZXh0
e30KYi5jb2RlcG9pbnRze0ZpYmVyLm5ld3t9LnRyYW5zZmVyKDAsMCwwLDAsMCwwLDAsMCwwLDAs
MCwwLDAsMCwwKX19fQ==' | base64 -d > poc
$ mruby poc
/home/faraday/mruby/src/vm.c:1929:16: runtime error: member access within misaligned address 0x000000000001 for type 'struct RArray', which requires 8 byte alignment
0x000000000001: note: pointer points here
<memory cannot be printed>
SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior /home/faraday/mruby/src/vm.c:1929:16 in 
AddressSanitizer:DEADLYSIGNAL
=================================================================
==36117==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000011 (pc 0x0000006f01ea bp 0x7fffb088c190 sp 0x7fffb086aa60 T0)
==36117==The signal is caused by a READ memory access.
==36117==Hint: address points to the zero page.
    #0 0x6f01ea in mrb_vm_exec /home/faraday/mruby/src/vm.c:1929:16
    #1 0x6b0ca9 in mrb_vm_run /home/faraday/mruby/src/vm.c:1130:12
    #2 0x6a5a79 in mrb_top_run /home/faraday/mruby/src/vm.c:3039:12
    #3 0x8b0ef1 in mrb_load_exec /home/faraday/mruby/mrbgems/mruby-compiler/core/parse.y:6890:7
    #4 0x8b2b56 in mrb_load_detect_file_cxt /home/faraday/mruby/mrbgems/mruby-compiler/core/parse.y:6933:12
    #5 0x4c6420 in main /home/faraday/mruby/mrbgems/mruby-bin-mruby/tools/mruby/mruby.c:357:11
    #6 0x7f8c3f9ff0b2 in __libc_start_main /build/glibc-eX1tMB/glibc-2.31/csu/../csu/libc-start.c:308:16
    #7 0x41c85d in _start (/home/faraday/mruby/build/host/bin/mruby+0x41c85d)

AddressSanitizer can not provide additional info.
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV /home/faraday/mruby/src/vm.c:1929:16 in mrb_vm_exec
==36117==ABORTING
Impact
This vulnerability is capable of making the mruby interpreter crash, thus affecting the availability of the system.

This bug was found by Octavio Gianatiempo (ogianatiempo@faradaysec.com) and Octavio Galland (ogalland@faradaysec.com) from Faraday Research Team.

payload.secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR imagemagick.cve-2018-5246..."
    # Execute the PoC to trigger the vulnerability
    /work/bin/magick montage /testcase/poc.pattern /dev/null
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/imagemagick
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    if /usr/local/bin/compile 1>/dev/null; then

    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR imagemagick.cve-2018-5248..."
    # Run the ImageMagick command to trigger the vulnerability
    touch /testcase/poc.sixel
    /src/imagemagick/utilities/magick montage /testcase/poc.sixel /dev/null
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/imagemagick
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

payload.bug_description: An invalid memory read (segmentation fault) occurs in internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs (src/lib/OpenEXRCore/validation.c). During header parsing (internal_exr_parse_header) the code invokes memcmp on attribute data that can reference out-of-bounds or uninitialized memory for crafted/malformed files, causing a crash. This can be triggered by attacker-supplied inputs and leads to denial-of-service during OpenEXR header validation.

payload.secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR libplist.cve-2017-5545..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /src/libplist/tools/plistutil -i /testcase/poc_short_file
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/libplist
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Ensure the script is executed with strict error handling
set -euo pipefail

# Define default CFLAGS if not set
CFLAGS="${CFLAGS:--O2}"

# Check if configure script exists and is executable
if [ -f ./configure ]; then
    chmod +x ./configure
    ./configure --static-build --extra-cflags="${CFLAGS}" --extra-ldflags="${CFLAGS}"
else
    echo "Error: configure script not found."
    exit 1
fi

# Compile the project using all available processors
make -j$(nproc)

Bool gf_sg_proto_field_is_sftime_offset(GF_Node *node, GF_FieldInfo *field)
{
    u32 i;
    GF_Route *r;
    GF_ProtoInstance *inst;
    GF_FieldInfo inf;
    if (node->sgprivate->tag != TAG_ProtoNode) return 0;
    if (field->fieldType != GF_SG_VRML_SFTIME) return 0;

    inst = (GF_ProtoInstance *) node;
    /*check in interface if this is ISed */
    i=0;
    while ((r = (GF_Route*)gf_list_enum(inst->proto_interface->sub_graph->Routes, &i))) {
        if (!r->IS_route) continue;
        /*only check eventIn/field/exposedField*/
        if (r->FromNode || (r->FromField.fieldIndex != field->fieldIndex)) continue;

        gf_node_get_field(r->ToNode, r->ToField.fieldIndex, &inf);   //  0x100
        /*IS to another proto*/
        if (r->ToNode->sgprivate->tag == TAG_ProtoNode) return gf_sg_proto_field_is_sftime_offset(r->ToNode, &inf);   // Recursive call triggered SIGSEGV
        /*IS to a startTime/stopTime field*/
        if (!stricmp(inf.name, "startTime") || !stricmp(inf.name, "stopTime")) return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR gpac.cve-2023-41000..."

patch() {

}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR libdwarf.cve-2022-34299..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /src/libdwarf-code/build/src/bin/dwarfdump/dwarfdump -vv -a /testcase/poc
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/libdwarf-code
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

payload.bug_description: Heap-use-after-free in xpath.c: xmlXPathNodeSetAdd (invoked via xmlXPathGetElementsByIds/xmlXPathIdFunction during XPath/XPointer evaluation) can access a node/attribute that was already freed while processing input (e.g. via xmlTextReader/XInclude). This results in reads of freed heap memory, leading to crashes and potential memory corruption when resolving ID-based references.

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /src/libxml2/xmllint --stream --xinclude /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/libxml2

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

payload.secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /src/libxml2/xmllint --html --maxmem 60000 /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/libxml2

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1

}

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules

        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    if /usr/local/bin/compile 1>/dev/null; then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR gpac.cve-2024-0322..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /src/gpac/bin/gcc/MP4Box -dash 1000 -out /dev/null /testcase/poc_1
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/gpac
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

build() {

    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi    
    
    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \n         1>/dev/null \n         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR libmodbus.cve-2022-0367..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability

    timeout 5s bash -c 'echo "A90AAAAN/xcBYgABAIQAAQLXEQ==" | base64 -d | nc 127.0.0.1 1502'

}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/libmodbus
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

payload.bug_description: A NULL/uninitialized-pointer dereference (segmentation fault) in urshift (mrbgems/mruby-bigint/core/bigint.c). urshift does not correctly handle zero-valued mpz_t operands and can read from an invalid/garbage limb pointer when performing right-shift operations (observed via mpz_div_2exp -> mrb_bint_rshift). This leads to a crash (invalid memory read) and can be triggered by crafted inputs, causing denial-of-service or other undefined behavior in mruby.
payload.build_sh:
#!/bin/bash
# Minimized build script with only core build commands
set -e

# Navigate to the mruby source directory
cd /src/mruby

# Set the linker to clang
export LD=clang

# Set linker flags
export LDFLAGS="-w -Wno-yacc -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types -fsanitize=address -fsanitize-address-use-after-scope"

# Build the project using rake with multiple processors
rake -m -j$(nproc)

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then

        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    USE_ZEND_ALLOC=0 /src/php-src/sapi/cli/php /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/php-src

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /src/mruby/build/host/bin/mruby /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/mruby

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"

        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

            build "$@"

        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /src/libxml2/xmllint --noout /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/libxml2

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

# Default build script template for C/C++ projects
set -eu

# Define configuration options
CONFIG_OPTS="--disable-shared"
CMAKE_OPTS="-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug"
MAKE_OPTS="-j$(nproc)"
BUILD_DIR="build"

# Set compiler flags
export CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -fsanitize=address"
export CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -fsanitize=address"

# 1. Run build preparation scripts if they exist
for prep_script in buildconf autogen.sh bootstrap; do
  if [ -x "$prep_script" ]; then
    echo "Running $prep_script..."
    ./$prep_script
    break
  elif [ -f "$prep_script" ]; then
    echo "Found $prep_script but it's not executable, setting permissions..."
    chmod +x $prep_script
    ./$prep_script
    break
  fi
done

# 2. Handle different build systems
if [ -f "configure" ]; then
  echo "Found configure script, running with options: $CONFIG_OPTS"
  ./configure $CONFIG_OPTS

  echo "Building with make $MAKE_OPTS"
  make $MAKE_OPTS
elif [ -f "CMakeLists.txt" ]; then
  echo "Found CMakeLists.txt, using CMake build system"
  mkdir -p $BUILD_DIR
  cd $BUILD_DIR
  cmake $CMAKE_OPTS ..
  make $MAKE_OPTS
elif [ -f "Makefile" ] || [ -f "makefile" ]; then
  echo "Found Makefile, building with make $MAKE_OPTS"
  make $MAKE_OPTS
elif [ -f "meson.build" ]; then
  echo "Found meson.build, using Meson build system"
  mkdir -p $BUILD_DIR
  meson setup $BUILD_DIR .
  cd $BUILD_DIR
  ninja
elif [ -f "GNUmakefile" ]; then
  echo "Found GNUmakefile, building with make $MAKE_OPTS"
  make $MAKE_OPTS
elif [ -d ".git" ] && [ -f "Makefile.am" ]; then
  echo "Found Makefile.am, running autoreconf"
  autoreconf -i
  ./configure $CONFIG_OPTS
  make $MAKE_OPTS
else
  echo "WARNING: No recognized build system found!"
  echo "Trying generic approach:"

  # Try to detect common source patterns and compile them
  if ls *.c >/dev/null 2>&1 || ls *.cpp >/dev/null 2>&1 || ls *.cc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Found C/C++ source files, attempting direct compilation"
    if ls *.cpp >/dev/null 2>&1 || ls *.cc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      CXX=${CXX:-g++}
      echo "Compiling C++ sources with $CXX"
      $CXX -g -O1 -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -o main *.cpp *.cc 2>/dev/null || true
    elif ls *.c >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      CC=${CC:-gcc}
      echo "Compiling C sources with $CC"
      $CC -g -O1 -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -o main *.c 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  fi
fi

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR imagemagick.cve-2019-13311..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /testcase/poc.sh
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/imagemagick
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/libheif
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    
    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi
    
    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with build."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi
    
    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \n         1>/dev/null \n         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR gpac.cve-2023-5586..."
    # Run the MP4Box command with the PoC file to trigger the vulnerability
    ./bin/gcc/MP4Box -dash 1000 -out /dev/null /testcase/poc2_null

    # The above command should trigger the AddressSanitizer error as described in the vulnerability report.
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/gpac
    
    # Check for repo_changes.diff and apply if it exists and hasn't been applied yet
    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then
        # Check if the patch has already been applied to avoid re-applying
        if ! git apply --check /testcase/repo_changes.diff &>/dev/null; then
            echo "Repository changes already applied or cannot be applied cleanly. Proceeding with patch."
        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi
    
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

    # stdout: /dev/null

    if [[ -f /testcase/repo_changes.diff ]]; then

        else
            echo "Applying repository changes from repo_changes.diff..."
            git apply /testcase/repo_changes.diff || echo "Warning: Could not apply repo_changes.diff cleanly. Proceeding anyway."
        fi
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \

        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    /src/njs/build/njs /testcase/poc
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."

    if [[ ! -f /testcase/model_patch.diff ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: /testcase/model_patch.diff not found. Please save the file before patching."
        exit 1
    fi

    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then

        exit 1

}


if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then

            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"

else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"

fi

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR gpac.cve-2023-4681..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /src/gpac/bin/gcc/MP4Box -dash 1000 /testcase/crash000004
    /src/gpac/bin/gcc/MP4Box -dash 1000 /testcase/crash000007
    /src/gpac/bin/gcc/MP4Box -dash 1000 /testcase/crash000014
    /src/gpac/bin/gcc/MP4Box -dash 1000 /testcase/crash000069
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/gpac
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

payload.bug_description: A malformed OpenEXR header can trigger an invalid memory read (segmentation fault / invalid pointer dereference) in internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs (src/lib/OpenEXRCore/validation.c). During header parsing (internal_exr_parse_header / exr_start_read), memcmp is called on attribute data that has not been properly validated, allowing crafted input to cause a crash/undefined behavior (denial-of-service).

    if /usr/local/bin/compile \

# ANALYSIS

The integer overflow issue exists in function bmptoimage. Here Info_h.biWidth == 0x40000001 and Info_h.biBitCount == 0x18 and stride should equals (0x40000001 \* 0x18 + 31) / 32 \* 4 == 0xC0000004. But actually stride equals 0x04 when overflow happened.

```
opj_image_t* bmptoimage(const char *filename, opj_cparameters_t *parameters)
{
    // ......
    stride = ((Info_h.biWidth * Info_h.biBitCount + 31U) / 32U) * 4U;
    if (Info_h.biBitCount == 4 && Info_h.biCompression == 2) { 
        stride = ((Info_h.biWidth * 8U + 31U) / 32U) * 4U;
    }
    pData = (OPJ_UINT8 *) calloc(1, stride * Info_h.biHeight * sizeof(OPJ_UINT8));
    if (pData == NULL) {
        fclose(IN);
        return NULL;
    }
    // ......
}
```
